subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should the cron agent tool expose flat `model`, `fallbacks`, and `toolsAllow` fields to models as accepted add/update shorthand, relying on the existing cron normalization and creator-tool allowlist cap?
rationale: The implementation is source-consistent and well tested, but the flat fields affect provider/model routing and tool-execution policy, which AGENTS.md marks as compatibility/security-sensitive maintainer territory.

options.title: Accept the flat surface
options.body: Merge the PR as a narrow repair for model-facing cron tool compatibility while keeping `contextTokens` and `maxSpendUsd` in the broader follow-up issue.

options.title: Narrow the flat surface
options.body: Ask the author to keep only schedule/message flat fields and leave provider/tool-control fields nested until a maintainer-approved schema policy is written.

options.title: Pause for broader design
options.body: Hold this PR until the remaining context-token and spend-cap cron contract is designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64721.

recommendation.title: Accept the flat surface
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as a narrow repair for model-facing cron tool compatibility while keeping `contextTokens` and `maxSpendUsd` in the broader follow-up issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the deepest recent history across cron tool schema, flat recovery, and runtime normalization, making him the best available routing owner for this boundary decision.
